units.title: Token-weighted loss denominators, microbatches, accumulation and seen-token counts
outcomes: Derive one token-weighted objective across uneven microbatches and a partial accumulation window.
Separate input tokens, valid loss tokens, attempted steps and successful optimizer updates.
Test a real trainer's denominator against a concatenated-batch gradient oracle.
units.why: The next-token objective is already familiar. Here the risk is a trainer that silently changes its weighting when masks, sequence lengths or accumulation change.

next.note: Apply exactly one optimizer update to the accumulated gradient.

study.title: OLMo-core: the effective-batch loss contract
study.locator: TransformerTrainModule.train_batch: label generation, batch_num_tokens_for_loss, instance_mask handling, microbatch splitting, summed loss and backward
study.depth: Read this single-device path, not pipeline parallelism. The instance-filter path deliberately includes excluded instances in the denominator; do not use that reported loss as the valid-token mean.

focus: Reuse The next-token objective: shifts, masks and perplexity. For this run, define the valid-token mask after shifting and packing, not from the raw input length.
For microbatch loss sums \(S_i\) and valid counts \(n_i\), backpropagate \(S_i/\sum_j n_j\). Averaging microbatch means is correct only when their valid counts are equal.
Log processed input tokens, valid targets and per-source exposure separately. A skipped optimizer update still consumed data and compute; it must not disappear from the ledger.
A zero-valid-token window has no mean objective. Reject or skip it explicitly before division, and record the decision.
units.reproduce: Closed-book, derive the loss for two microbatches with loss sums 4 and 6 and valid counts 2 and 6: the token mean is 1.25, not the mean-of-means 1.5. Then use PyTorch 2.14.1 on CPU to compare summed-loss accumulation with concatenated-batch gradients on fixed logits with unequal masks. Disable dropout and use explicit floating-point tolerances.
traps: Dividing every microbatch by the configured accumulation length when the final window is shorter. Normalize by the actual valid count in that window.
Calling nanoGPT's last-microbatch training loss the effective-batch loss. Accumulate detached loss sums and counts for logging too.
Assuming input tokens equal supervised targets. Padding, ignored labels and boundary policies can make those counts different.

selfTest.q: Why does doubling a short microbatch's padding change a mean-of-means trainer but not the intended objective?
selfTest.a: Its microbatch mean receives the same weight despite having fewer valid targets. Summing valid losses and dividing once by the total count preserves token weighting.

selfTest.q: One device processes two sequences of length 64 per microbatch, with four microbatches per update. What can you count without inspecting labels?
selfTest.a: 512 input-token positions per attempted update. The valid-target count needs the shifted-label mask, and the successful-update count needs the optimizer outcome.

selfTest.q: When should full-batch and accumulated gradients agree?
selfTest.a: When they evaluate the same additive objective at the same weights with the same data and stochastic choices, without batch-dependent operations or intermediate updates. Floating-point reduction order still permits small differences.

practice.name: TensorTonic: Gradient Accumulation Equivalence
practice.locator: Implement gradient_accumulation_step; public cases Uneven microbatches, Two equal microbatches and Zero loss
practice.note: The free problem weights linear-model squared error by examples, not language-model tokens. Transfer its denominator argument to valid targets in lmlab and add a partial-window test; the public cases do not test masking or autograd gradients.

units.stopWhen: The public cases pass, and your masked accumulated gradient matches the concatenated oracle within a stated tolerance, including an uneven final window and explicit empty-window handling.

fit.note: Kept: OLMo-core exposes the denominator and microbatch path; the free named drill plus lmlab's masked oracle supplies the research-depth check.

units.title: AdamW state, parameter groups, weight decay and update-to-weight ratios
outcomes: Audit parameter groups for missing, duplicate and unintentionally decayed parameters, including tied weights.
Explain an observed update using moments, bias correction, decay and the learning-rate history.
Measure update-to-weight ratios without mistaking gradient norms for parameter changes.
units.why: AdamW, schedules and the global token batch supplied the update equations. Research comparisons now need evidence that every named parameter received the intended update and retained the right state.

next.note: Keep the update ledger when changing schedule or batch size.

study.title: CS336 Spring 2026 Assignment 1: inspect your existing AdamW
study.locator: Version 26.0.3, Section 4.3: Algorithm 1 and problems adamw and adamw_accounting
study.depth: Do not rebuild the foundation optimizer. Use the equations to audit the implementation and state you will actually train with.

study.title: OLMo-core: stateful and skipped AdamW updates
study.locator: adamw_step and SkipStepAdamW._step: step_factor, exp_avg, exp_avg_sq, bias correction and step_increment_bugfix
study.depth: Follow the scalar path; skip foreach_adamw_step. The skip-step policy is a case study, not a requirement to adopt it.

focus: Keep a table of parameter names, tensor identities, shapes, decay settings and learning rates. A tied embedding and output head share one parameter, not two optimizer entries.
Compare \(\|	heta_{t+1}-	heta_t\|_2/\|	heta_t\|_2\) per group or layer. Mark a zero denominator as undefined and log the absolute update instead.
Measure the actual before-and-after parameter delta. Adam's preconditioning, decay and clipping make the gradient norm an inadequate proxy.
Distinguish a missing gradient from a zero gradient. With PyTorch 2.14.1 AdamW, a parameter with `grad=None` is skipped; a zero tensor can still produce decay and momentum-driven updates.
units.reproduce: On CPU with PyTorch 2.14.1, take one float64 AdamW step from weight 2 and gradient 3, with learning rate 0.1, betas `(0.9, 0.99)`, epsilon `1e-8` and weight decay 0.1. Derive first moment 0.3, second moment 0.09 and new weight about 1.8800000003. The total update-to-weight ratio is about 0.06. Compare a second step with and without the saved moments, using the same next gradient.
traps: Calling decoupled weight decay an extra loss gradient. It acts outside Adam's adaptive denominator.
Loading optimizer state into a differently ordered parameter-group layout. Matching shapes alone does not prove the moments belong to the same parameter.
Treating one update-ratio threshold as universal across embeddings, norms and hidden matrices. Keep layerwise baselines and investigate changes.

selfTest.q: A parameter has zero current gradient but moves. Is that necessarily a bug?
selfTest.a: No. Stored momentum and decoupled decay can both move it. Inspect the moments, decay and actual gradient representation before diagnosing it.

selfTest.q: Two layers have equal gradient norms. Must their update-to-weight ratios match?
selfTest.a: No. Their moment histories, weight norms, group learning rates and decay can differ.

selfTest.q: Why is a weights-only restart not the same AdamW experiment?
selfTest.a: It resets the moments and step counters, hence the adaptive direction and bias corrections. Even identical next data and learning rate do not recover the original update.

practice.name: CS336 Assignment 1: adamw regression audit
practice.locator: test_adamw and its _optimize helper; connect your optimizer through get_adamw_cls
practice.note: The public test compares the final linear-model weights after 1000 updates against PyTorch or a snapshot with tolerance; it does not audit parameter groups or resume. Add those checks in lmlab. The handout and tests are public study material; never publish assignment solutions.

units.stopWhen: The scalar update and public regression agree within declared tolerances, and every trainable tensor appears once in a named group with a recorded actual update ratio.

fit.note: Kept: CS336 anchors the update oracle and public regression; OLMo-core exposes the state and skipped-update mechanism for the lmlab audit.

units.title: Warmup-stable-decay schedules, gradient noise and the critical batch
outcomes: Specify warmup, stable and decay phases with unambiguous step and token boundaries.
Explain the critical batch as an optimization trade-off, not a memory-capacity limit.
Compare schedule and batch interventions under fixed tokens, held-out evaluation and recorded seed variation.
units.why: A stable-phase checkpoint can support several cooldown experiments, but those branches still cost tokens and compute. This unit makes that reuse explicit instead of treating a paper's schedule as a universal recipe.

next.note: Study how batch and learning-rate transfer limits confound scaling comparisons.

study.title: Constant learning rate plus cooldown
study.locator: Sections 2 and 3, especially 3.1 Advantages of Constant Learning Rates and 3.2 Experimental Comparison, Figures 3 to 6
study.depth: Stop before stochastic weight averaging. Treat the 210M SlimPajama comparisons as the authors' evidence, not a target for your decoder.

study.title: MiniCPM: the WSD contract
study.locator: Section 4.2 WSD LRS, Equation 1; Section 4.3 and its decay-stage experiments
study.depth: Read the schedule and branch-reuse argument only. Do not reproduce MiniCPM's model-scale runs.

study.title: Noise scale and the useful-batch frontier
study.locator: Figure 1; Sections 2.1 to 2.3, especially Equations 2.2, 2.8 and 2.12
study.depth: Stop after the steps-versus-examples trade-off. Full noise-scale estimation and large-batch theory are depth, not the exit gate.

focus: Write which learning rate is used by each attempted update and whether the schedule advances on attempted or successful updates. Record both counters and the consumed-token position.
WSD names phases, not one decay function. The TensorTonic drill uses endpoint-inclusive cosine decay; MiniCPM permits a decreasing decay function and Hagele studies linear and square-root cooldowns.
The paper's inverse-batch covariance law assumes independent samples. Adjacent language-model tokens are correlated; report your batch unit and do not call a token count an independent-sample count.

At fixed tokens, a larger batch gives fewer updates. Retune learning rate with the same small search budget, and compare held-out loss after cooldown, not an unannealed branch against an annealed one.
units.reproduce: Derive the free WSD drill's six rates for total steps 6, warmup steps 2, stable steps 2, peak rate 1 and final ratio 0: `[0.5, 1, 1, 1, 1, 0]`. Explain why its one-step decay uses the final rate immediately. In lmlab, fork one saved stable-phase state into constant and cooldown branches with identical next tokens and held-out evaluation; keep both outcomes rather than requiring cooldown to win.
traps: Counting a reused prefix once in every branch's independent-run cost, or counting all cooldown branches as free. Report shared cost, marginal branch cost and total study cost separately.
Calling the largest batch that fits memory the critical batch. One is a system limit; the other concerns diminishing optimization returns.
Transferring a source's decay fraction without checking your budget, data and optimizer. Tiny-scale evidence supports only the tested regime.

selfTest.q: Why can a stable-phase checkpoint be more useful for continued training than its cooled-down descendant?
selfTest.a: It preserves the high-rate trajectory. Continuing the cooled-down state at a high rate introduces a rewarming intervention whose stability and forgetting need separate testing.

selfTest.q: Why can doubling batch size reduce steps without reducing total tokens to a given loss?
selfTest.a: Larger gradients are less noisy but have diminishing per-step benefit. The step saving may be smaller than the doubled examples per step.

selfTest.q: If the token batch doubles at a fixed token budget, what happens to the number of optimizer opportunities?
selfTest.a: It roughly halves, with rounding and the final partial batch handled explicitly. This changes the optimization horizon even before considering skipped steps.

practice.name: TensorTonic: Generate a Warmup-Stable-Decay Schedule
practice.locator: Implement wsd_learning_rate; public cases Warmup stable and two-step decay, No warmup and One-step decay
practice.note: The free cases check specific rate vectors, not learning quality. The section mini-project adds a fixed-token schedule fork and a small batch-size comparison on your decoder, using three paired seeds and a fixed held-out slice. On CPU, shorten context and the common token budget for every arm equally.

units.stopWhen: The boundary cases pass, and your branch ledger accounts for all consumed tokens, successful updates and shared versus marginal cost, with held-out outcomes and seed spread for the small comparisons.

fit.note: Kept: the two schedule papers supply the method, McCandlish supplies the critical-batch assumptions, and the free drill plus bounded lmlab comparisons fit the gate.

units.title: Mixed precision, loss scaling, nonfinite handling and gradient-clipping placement
outcomes: Integrate autocast, token-normalized accumulation, unscaling and clipping at effective-batch boundaries.
Reject nonfinite updates while retaining the offending batch and precision-state evidence.
Record the actual parameter, gradient, moment and accumulation dtypes rather than assuming them from the precision label.
units.why: Mixed precision, autocast and gradient scaling are prerequisites. The new contract is their interaction with uneven accumulation, skipped updates, schedule position and recoverable language-model state.

next.note: Capture the first numerical event before it becomes a loss spike.

study.title: Mixed Precision Training: the three numerical safeguards
study.locator: Sections 3.1 FP32 Master Copy of Weights, 3.2 Loss Scaling and 3.3 Arithmetic Precision, plus Figure 1
study.depth: Stop before the benchmark results. This is the FP16 rationale, not a claim that every current BF16 implementation uses the same storage layout.

study.title: PyTorch 2.14 AMP: clipping and accumulation
study.locator: Typical Mixed Precision Training; Working with Unscaled Gradients - Gradient clipping; Working with Scaled Gradients - Gradient accumulation
study.depth: Use the single-optimizer path. Replace division by the configured accumulation length with the actual valid-token denominator from the first unit.

focus: With PyTorch 2.14.1, keep the scaler's scale fixed throughout an accumulation window. Unscale once after its last backward, inspect finiteness, record the unclipped norm, clip, then perform the conditional step and scale update.
FP32 parameters under autocast retain FP32 leaf gradients and normally FP32 AdamW moments. Autocast does not itself convert the stored parameters to BF16 or create an extra persistent master copy.

BF16's exponent range usually removes the need for scaling, not the need for finiteness checks. Use FP32 on CPU if BF16 operations are unsupported; a CPU `torch.amp.GradScaler('cpu')` can test skip semantics without requiring FP16 kernels.
Keep consumed-token counters even when the optimizer skips. Log scale, pre-clip norm, skip decision and schedule position so a resume preserves the chosen policy.
units.reproduce: On CPU with PyTorch 2.14.1, give an SGD parameter gradient `[3.0, 4.0]` through a loss scaled by 8. Unscale, record norm 5, then clip with maximum norm 1; the result is approximately `[0.6, 0.8]` within `1e-6`. Repeat with one infinite gradient using `torch.amp.GradScaler('cpu', init_scale=8.0)`: the parameter must not change and the default scale update reduces the scale to 4. Do not clip the invalid gradient before recording it.
traps: Unscaling each microbatch separately. Later scaled gradients then accumulate into unscaled buffers and cannot be interpreted with one scale.
Using the return value of `scaler.step(optimizer)` as a universal success flag. Most optimizer steps return `None` even on success; instrument the actual step decision.
Clipping each microbatch instead of the accumulated gradient. Clipping is nonlinear, so that trains a different update.

selfTest.q: Why is clipping before unscaling wrong?
selfTest.a: The threshold is applied to the scaled norm. After unscaling, the effective clipping threshold is smaller by the scale factor.

selfTest.q: A scaler skipped an update. Should you replay the batch automatically?
selfTest.a: Not silently. Replaying changes data exposure and cost. Follow the run's declared skip or replay policy, and record the consumed tokens and every attempt either way.

selfTest.q: Does enabling BF16 autocast guarantee that accumulation uses BF16?
selfTest.a: No. FP32 leaf parameters normally accumulate FP32 gradients. Inspect actual buffers and optimizer state; operation precision and stored-state precision are different choices.

units.practiceNote: The section mini-project covers this: the mixed-precision accumulation path, one seeded nonfinite event, a refused update and a precision-state resume regression in lmlab.
units.stopWhen: Your finite accumulated update matches an FP32 control within a declared tolerance, and an injected nonfinite gradient leaves parameters and optimizer moments unchanged while the event and counters remain recorded.

fit.note: Currency and coverage failed for effective-batch scaling and current skip semantics. The opened PyTorch 2.14 AMP examples fill that gap beside the original precision paper.

units.title: Initialization transfer and muP width-scaling rules
outcomes: Derive width multipliers for input, hidden and output weights under one stated muP convention.
Distinguish transferable optimization hyperparameters from regularization choices that need new evidence.
Specify a width-transfer control that keeps architecture, depth, data and optimization budget comparable.
units.why: Initialization at one width is not a scaling rule. A research program needs a family of parameterizations whose learning-rate transfer can be tested, not a copied learning rate from a smaller model.

next.note: Test the limits of width transfer before using it to allocate a scaling budget.

study.title: Tensor Programs V: muTransfer and explicit width rules
study.locator: Algorithm 1 and Table 1; Section 4, Table 3 and Equations 3 and 4 for the MLP; Figure 1 for Transformer learning-rate transfer; Section 6.1 for caveats
study.depth: Use the Table 3 convention for the derivation. Stop before the general proof in Appendix J. A decoder with tied embeddings needs the compatible convention in Table 8, not a direct copy of the untied MLP rules.

focus: Table 3 states initialization variances, not standard deviations. A hidden-weight variance proportional to \(1/n\) gives standard deviation proportional to \(1/\sqrt{n}\); the output-weight variance there scales as \(1/n^2\).
Separate the tuned base learning rate from width-dependent group multipliers. Input, hidden and output matrices do not all receive one identical Adam learning rate under Table 3.
muP is a joint initialization, parameterization and update-scaling contract. Changing only initialization is not muTransfer; Transformer attention and tied weights introduce further rules.
Table 1 does not promise transfer of dropout or weight decay. Keep fixed-depth, fixed-data width tests separate from claims about depth, sequence length or a new optimizer.
units.reproduce: Closed-book, widen the equal-hidden-width MLP in Equation 4 from its base width by a factor of 4, keeping input and output dimensions fixed. Hidden-weight initialization standard deviation halves and output-weight standard deviation quarters. Under its SGD convention, input-weight and hidden-bias learning rates multiply by 4, hidden-weight learning rate stays fixed and output-weight learning rate divides by 4. Then read Table 3's Adam row: input weights and biases keep their rates, while hidden and output weight rates divide by 4. State the convention before each comparison.
traps: Applying a variance multiplier directly to the initialization standard deviation. Take the square root first.
Using the Table 3 output-weight rule with a separately scaled readout from another convention. Equivalent parameterizations require consistent forward and optimizer transformations.
Calling stable activation magnitudes proof that the best learning rate transfers. A coordinate-scale check and a held-out optimization comparison answer different questions.

selfTest.q: Why are width-independent initial activations insufficient to establish useful width transfer?
selfTest.a: They constrain the initial forward pass, not the sizes and effects of learned updates. The optimizer and parameterization must also scale appropriately.

selfTest.q: Can a transferred base learning rate imply different actual learning rates for two matrix groups?
selfTest.a: Yes. The base hyperparameter can stay fixed while prescribed width multipliers change each group's rate.

selfTest.q: A learning rate transferred across two widths. Does the result establish transfer to a deeper decoder or a new tokenizer?
selfTest.a: No. Those changes alter the tested family or data representation. They need separate controlled evidence.

units.practiceNote: The section mini-project covers this: a width-rule worksheet for the chosen decoder and a bounded initialization-transfer check, with actual parameter-group multipliers and activation scales saved alongside the run contract.
units.stopWhen: You derive the fourfold-width multipliers without the table, identify your decoder's tied-weight and attention conventions, and separate a scale check from evidence of optimal-hyperparameter transfer.

fit.note: Kept: Algorithm 1, Tables 1 and 3 and Equation 4 supply transfer vocabulary and explicit derive-level rules; the lmlab worksheet prevents an unsupported decoder-wide substitution.

units.title: Versioned run contracts, deterministic smoke tests, overfit checks and stop rules
outcomes: Implement a versioned run contract binding corpus, tokenizer, model, objective, optimizer, precision and evaluator identity.
Gate launches on deterministic smoke tests and a separate overfit-one-batch diagnostic.
Declare budgets, validation cadence, stop triggers and rollback ownership before comparing configurations.
units.why: The lmlab run is now an experiment, not just a training script. A frozen contract makes later changes to data, schedule, resume and evaluation visible rather than silently redefining the baseline.

next.note: Make the run contract enforceable at save and load boundaries.

study.title: Specify the comparison before launching it
study.locator: Identifying scientific, nuisance, and fixed hyperparameters; Determining the number of steps for each training run; Saving checkpoints and retrospectively selecting the best checkpoint; Setting up experiment tracking
study.depth: Skip batch-normalization guidance. Here compute-limited means budget-limited training, not evidence that GPU kernels are compute-bound.

study.title: OLMo-core: a bounded CPU integration configuration
study.locator: build_config and test_train_small_model_cpu: olmo3_30M, sequence length 64, five steps and model-merge/load checks
study.depth: Read as the reference contract. Running the OLMo test is optional: it needs extra dependencies and external data. Do not launch the official large-model scripts.

study.title: CS336 Spring 2026 Assignment 1: launch and overfit checks
study.locator: Version 26.0.3, Section 5.3 Training loop and Section 7.2.3 Tips and tricks for debugging model architectures
study.depth: Use your existing decoder on a small versioned corpus slice. Replace the assignment's full training and leaderboard budgets with minutes-long smoke runs; do not adopt its score targets or publish solutions.

focus: Reuse Objective checks, tiny-set overfit and shuffled-label controls. A smoke run checks finite state and reproducible execution; overfitting one batch tests whether the implementation can learn its targets, not generalization.

Record code revision, dependency versions, data and tokenizer hashes, model shape, masks, groups, schedule units, RNG streams, checkpoint policy and the fixed held-out evaluation slice. Pin this training path to PyTorch 2.14.1.

Use your LMR-2 decoder around 10M parameters for the small study. If it does not fit your GPU, use shorter context and smaller microbatches; a two-layer, width-64 decoder with a small vocabulary on CPU suffices for contract and failure tests.

Predeclare token and wall-time budgets, nonfinite refusal, identity-mismatch refusal, validation selection and rollback rules. A changed contract starts a named branch with a parent checkpoint, not an invisible continuation.
units.reproduce: From the same initial state, run five updates twice on an immutable small token fixture with fixed batches and a deterministic CPU path. Compare the batch identities, losses, optimizer counters and final tensors. Separately repeat one fixed batch with dropout and decay disabled until its loss falls substantially; save the curve as a diagnostic, and evaluate the actual study only on held-out documents. A constant-sequence fixture is acceptable for this test, not for a quality claim.
traps: Expecting every overfit-one-batch run to reach zero loss. Conflicting targets for identical available contexts can impose a nonzero optimum; choose a learnable diagnostic fixture.
Selecting checkpoints on the final test set. Use a development slice for selection and reserve an untouched evaluation slice for the frozen result.
Trusting nanoGPT's `max_iters` as an update count. At the pinned revision its loop executes `max_iters + 1` updates; test and fix your stop boundary.

selfTest.q: The batch overfit check passes. What has not been established?
selfTest.a: Generalization, correct data order over a full run, resume equivalence and fairness of later comparisons. A model can memorize a flawed diagnostic batch.

selfTest.q: Why distinguish a budget stop from a numerical stop?
selfTest.a: The first completes the planned exposure; the second is a failed or interrupted attempt. Combining them hides instability and makes completed-run averages misleading.

selfTest.q: You double the batch while leaving maximum steps fixed. Is that the same token-budget experiment?
selfTest.a: No. It roughly doubles data exposure. Recompute steps or explicitly change the comparison contract.

units.practiceNote: The section mini-project covers this: lmlab's frozen baseline manifest, deterministic launch gate, learnable single-batch overfit check, fixed held-out evaluation and tested stop/rollback policy.
units.stopWhen: A clean invocation reproduces the smoke trace at the declared equivalence level, the separate learnable fixture overfits, and an exceeded budget or identity mismatch triggers the declared stop with evidence retained.

fit.note: Kept: the Playbook defines comparison discipline, CS336 defines the small-loop controls, and OLMo-core supplies a real integration configuration without making its dependency stack mandatory.

units.title: Complete language-model checkpoint state, atomic publication and corrupted-state handling
outcomes: Map every mutable language-model training state to its owner and serialized representation.
Publish immutable local checkpoints with integrity metadata and an explicit reader acceptance rule.
Reject incomplete, corrupted or incompatible state before mutating the live training objects.
units.why: Complete checkpoints and atomic writes are familiar. This unit audits a real trainer, extends a deliberately incomplete one, and proves that interruption and corruption cannot silently select an invalid continuation.

next.note: Test that accepted state actually continues the same experiment.

study.title: OLMo-core: trainer state versus model and optimizer state
study.locator: Trainer.state_dict, load_state_dict and load_checkpoint: counters, loader, callbacks and conditional RNG restoration
study.depth: Do not mistake Trainer.state_dict alone for the full checkpoint; model and optimizer state belong to the train module.

study.title: OLMo-core: local publication and discovery
study.locator: Checkpointer.save, dir_is_checkpoint, find_checkpoints, latest_checkpoint, _save_metadata, _get_tmp_dir and _teardown_tmp_dir
study.depth: Trace local storage only. Remote uploads do not inherit local atomic-rename semantics; sharding and fleet recovery stay outside this section.

study.title: nanoGPT: the checkpoint to extend
study.locator: init_from == 'resume' branch; scaler creation; checkpoint dictionary and torch.save inside the evaluation branch; initial and prefetched X, Y batches

study.title: Local atomic replacement and synchronization
study.locator: os.replace and os.fsync entries, including the same-filesystem restriction and flush-before-fsync instruction (page read 2026-10-16)

focus: Save at a completed-update boundary: model, moments and group mapping, schedule position, scaler, counters, CPU and device RNG, sampler/shuffle state, corpus/tokenizer/config hashes and callback state. Mid-accumulation saves additionally need partial gradients and window position.

nanoGPT does not save RNG, scaler or loader state. Its random-window sampler also prefetches the next batch before saving; either save that pending batch and its identity or move publication to a boundary with a fully specified next-batch recipe.

For local single-file checkpoints, write an immutable payload through a temporary sibling, flush and synchronize it, then atomically replace its final name. Publish a manifest last with size, digest, schema and run identity; readers require all checks before loading into fresh objects.

A successful rename gives atomic visibility, not guaranteed survival of power loss. Directory synchronization and filesystem behavior matter for durability. Keep the previous verified checkpoint until the new one has passed validation.
units.reproduce: In a CPU test, retain one verified checkpoint, start a separate writer for the next temporary payload, and terminate it after it signals that only part was written. Discovery must ignore that unpublished attempt. Next, alter one byte in a copied published payload without updating its recorded digest: validation must reject it before deserialization or live-state mutation. Keep both failure records and show explicit fallback to the older verified state.
traps: Calling successful deserialization an integrity check. Corrupted tensor bytes may still deserialize; validate the recorded digest and semantic identity too.
Using a filename or modification time as proof of completeness. Select the highest accepted step with its manifest, not merely the newest path.
Treating an in-memory state dictionary as an immutable snapshot. Its tensors can alias live state; serialize immediately or copy them before training continues.

selfTest.q: The model and optimizer reload correctly. Why might the next training batch still be wrong?
selfTest.a: The loader position, random stream or already-prefetched batch may be missing. A checkpoint must describe the next consumed batch, not only the last completed update.

selfTest.q: A checkpoint's checksum passes, but its tokenizer hash differs. May you resume it as the same run?
selfTest.a: No. Integrity proves the bytes match the manifest, not that the bytes belong to a compatible experiment. Reject the mismatch or declare an explicit new intervention.

selfTest.q: Can an atomic rename alone guarantee a checkpoint survives sudden power loss?
selfTest.a: No. Visibility and durability are different guarantees. Buffered data and directory entries need appropriate synchronization, with filesystem-specific limits.

units.practiceNote: The section mini-project covers this: extend the pinned nanoGPT checkpoint path in lmlab with complete state, immutable publication, a manifest, kill-during-save and corruption tests, and explicit last-good fallback.
units.stopWhen: Interrupted publication, byte tampering and tokenizer/config mismatches are rejected without changing live state, and the previous verified checkpoint remains loadable.

fit.note: Coverage failed for the local replace and synchronization API guarantees. Python's opened os reference fills that gap; OLMo-core and nanoGPT remain the state and extension case studies.

units.title: Exact and statistical resume equivalence, and data discontinuity diagnostics
outcomes: Specify exact, tolerance-based and statistical continuation criteria before running a restart test.
Compare next-batch identities, RNG-dependent computation, optimizer state and held-out loss across a process restart.
Localize a data discontinuity to corpus, shard, tokenizer, mixture, sequence-length or sampler-state changes.
units.why: A smooth loss curve is weak evidence of correct resume. Token exposure can repeat or skip without a conspicuous spike, so continuation must be checked against an uninterrupted trace at the same logical position.

next.note: Use batch and state alignment to distinguish a resume defect from optimization failure.

study.title: OLMo-core: loader fingerprint and consumed position
study.locator: NumpyDataLoaderBase.state_dict and load_state_dict: dataset_fingerprint_version, dataset_fingerprint, batches_processed, tokens_processed, seed and epoch
study.depth: Notice that a fingerprint-version mismatch only warns, while a same-version fingerprint mismatch normally raises. Make lmlab's strict acceptance policy explicit rather than assuming both cases fail closed.

study.title: OLMo-core: RNG restoration boundary
study.locator: Trainer.load_state_dict: loader restoration, callback state, matching-world-size RNG restore and library-version warning

study.title: Recognize resume and repetition patterns
study.locator: Resume-related spikes: DataSampler related issues and Impacts of repeat data
study.depth: Treat the historical framework anecdotes as cases, not current universal defaults. Use batch lineage to test your loader directly.

focus: Compare the resumed run with the uninterrupted suffix, including the first consumed batch, valid-target count, learning rate, scaler, moments and parameter tensors. Evaluation must not perturb the training RNG stream unnoticed.

Exact equivalence means bitwise state and trace agreement within a frozen deterministic environment. Tolerance-based numerical agreement is a different claim; cross-release or cross-device identity is not promised by PyTorch.

For an explicitly nondeterministic path, compare paired multi-seed held-out results and diagnostics against a prespecified practical margin. An insignificant difference or one similar curve is not proof of statistical equivalence.
Log source, shard, token offsets, tokenizer hash, packing version, sequence length and batch digest. A corpus fingerprint alone does not certify every tokenizer or packing choice.
units.reproduce: Using PyTorch 2.14.1 on CPU, run your tiny decoder with nonzero dropout and fixed data order. Save after three completed updates, continue two more as the reference, then terminate and resume fresh objects in a new process for those same two updates. Restore RNG only after object construction and loader setup. Require exact batch identities and bitwise tensor agreement on this deterministic path. Repeat with RNG restoration omitted and with the sampler reset; your checks must identify the earliest differing stream, not merely the final loss.
traps: Treating statistical equivalence as permission for repeated or missing documents. Logical data identity remains testable even when kernels are nondeterministic.
Restoring RNG before constructing the model. Initialization consumes draws and shifts the resumed stochastic stream.
Ignoring a fingerprint mismatch because the validation curve seems healthy. That turns a continuation into an undocumented data intervention.

selfTest.q: Batch hashes match after resume, but dropout outputs differ immediately. What do you inspect first?
selfTest.a: The relevant RNG state and restoration order, train/eval mode and deterministic execution settings. Matching data does not imply matching stochastic computation.

selfTest.q: Why can a reset sampler initially improve the training loss?
selfTest.a: It can replay already-learned examples. Lower replay loss is not evidence of better generalization or correct exposure.

selfTest.q: Three seeds show no statistically significant loss difference. Have you proved equivalence?
selfTest.a: No. Failure to detect a difference can reflect low power. Specify a meaningful equivalence margin and report the uncertainty relative to it, while checking deterministic state and lineage directly.

units.practiceNote: The section mini-project covers this: an uninterrupted-versus-killed-process continuation test with dropout, missing-RNG and repeated-shard negative controls, plus strict data/tokenizer/config fingerprint failures.
units.stopWhen: A real restart passes the declared equivalence contract, and the omitted-RNG, reset-sampler and changed-identity controls fail at the expected boundary with the earliest differing evidence preserved.

fit.note: Kept: OLMo-core exposes restoration and fingerprint limits; Stas supplies discontinuity cases, while the lmlab restart campaign supplies the missing executable equivalence test.
